title: Week 1 of Agentic Trading mostly through Robinhood Agentic
author: randbobaccount
selftext:
Been running 13 autonomous agents on a live account across Robinhood, coinbase and Kalshi, each with its own capital slice and no coordination layer between them. Up 6.97% this week overall.

Some of the designs:

Truth Social, inverted. An LLM scores every new Trump post for directional tone with a 0 to 1 confidence. Acts only above 0.8, then inverts the call. High confidence bullish rotates to TLT/GLD, high confidence bearish to SPY/QQQ. Below threshold, nothing happens.

Same feed, patient. A second agent waits five days after a post before acting, on the theory that the first two sessions are reaction and whatever is left after that is the real move. Longer holds. Running both is how I am trying to find out whether the signal is in the reaction or in what survives it.

ClinicalTrials.gov. Buys a whitelisted biotech sponsor when a trial registers a Phase 3 entry, holds 60 days. Favourite idea in here, because the source is a government registry nobody is racing to price.

STOCK Act disclosures. Mirrors purchase filings from a set of high-volume House and Senate filers. Next bar, 60 day hold, capped at 8 concurrent.

Crypto, winner take all. Ten liquid Coinbase pairs ranked every day on 7 day momentum, volume trend and volatility. It holds the single highest-conviction coin and nothing else, re-picked daily. Zero diversification by design, but it’s been performing well.

Kalshi versus the forecasters. Compares Kalshi economic-data prices against figures institutions have already published (Cleveland Fed nowcast, wire consensus, CME FedWatch) and acts only when the two disagree by a real margin. It does not forecast anything itself. Not seeing good results on Kalshi. 

Plus a sector contrarian that buys the two weakest of the 11 S&P sectors, a WallStreetBets agent weighted by sentiment times upvotes, and two crypto rotations.

First week is in the screenshots. Way too early to read anything into it.

Still working out: 

One, overlap. 13 agents running independently with nothing netting them, and several keep landing on the same names from completely different logic. I think I am diversified across 13 strategies and I genuinely do not know how concentrated I actually am. Is there a good way to measure that across agents without just collapsing everything into one portfolio?

Two, the confidence threshold. The Trump agent only acts above 0.8. I picked 0.8 by feel. Does anyone actually calibrate this, as in check whether the model is right 80% of the time when it says 0.8, and set the cutoff from that? Or is everyone eyeballing it.

What would you add?

comments.author: istockustock
comments.body: how often are the trades placed?. Also, How different is this from Autopilot?

replies.author: randbobaccount
replies.body:
It depends on the agents. Either daily, hourly, or when events come in they “wake up” and find the target portfolio. Sometimes trading, sometimes not if it’s the same. 

Autopilot charges an insane amount - wouldn’t be profitable even if they gave me insane returns (I tried it out and was down…). Also felt like a scam to me when I used it, they connect to the brokerage with a phishing link. Overall they’re more just copy trading with some overall Ai strats, but it’s always following instead of a fair distribution. Raijin has strats for a ton of ideas, honest live performance, and I can just make my own algos relatively easily on the app.

replies.author: FlabbyLabby
replies.body: Just FYI, Raijin warns that autonomous agents can suffer from model error, stale feeds/API failures and runaway execution, and recommends hard position, drawdown, scope and kill-switch controls. So, the AI telemetry is still off.

replies.author: Newrateacc
replies.body: Interesting. Looks like they automatically setup those risk levers like stop loss and kill switch for us. So I think the strategy will switch to cash if things start crashing.

comments.author: Weird_Cookie1700
comments.body:
https://reddit.com/link/p26czxr/video/bi50izrlruhh1/player

  
I made a game that uses an AI I named Charles, he’s pretty good at predicting the movement for the day.

I also made a few agents that trade on alpaca, they’re kinda useless though. They’re real hit or miss. I did actually use the engine for the predictions for a little bit to see how that worked and it was nice.

Right now I’m just manual trading during the day and have an overnight agent that buys at 355pm and I manually sell that at 930am the next morning or the AI does if it hits 2.5% after 930am but before I sell it (sometimes a 2 is just as good as a 2.5)

replies.author: randbobaccount
replies.body: Nice, have you tried building our Charles on an official trading app? Would be cool if it worked on Raijin itself

replies.author: Weird_Cookie1700
replies.body:
Building it on an app? No, there’s no way I could do that, he’s far too advanced. Right now there are a few different versions of Charles but there’s one we have running on Robinhood and 2 that we have running on Alpaca.

The Alpaca ones are just test accounts right now until we get the algos right, the Robinhood one is alright and we use it nightly. 

Hopefully that answers your question?

If you're looking to do something more high frequency in the future that works on a per-second basis, you could check out Everstrike.
